stories.title: Startup Spotlight: Porchlight uses AI to help foster human connection in senior care
stories.summary: A one-person Seattle startup called Porchlight is using AI to help caregivers actually know the people they care for. Residents tap a button, answer a question, and their memories get turned into a 'Know Your Resident' briefing — so a former machinist or dancer isn't just a room number. Founder Patrick Donahue built it after his father's death, asking how much of a person's story goes with them unless someone asks in time.
stories.extended_summary: Patrick Donahue watched his father die and couldn't shake one question: how much of a person's story goes with them unless someone asks while there's still time? So the Seattle software engineer built Porchlight — a tool where a memory care resident taps one button, hears a question, and records a memory. AI transcription turns those answers into a 'Know Your Resident' briefing, so every caregiver walks in already knowing the former machinist, the dancer, the veteran. Families get a private audio page to listen and reply. Donahue deliberately stripped marketing claims off his own site when they described features he hadn't built yet, and keeps the tool free while communities test it. His line: 'Nothing in it pretends to be a person.'
